critical_findings.finding: The published SCADA measurement files (2018_SCADA_*.csv / .xlsx, 2019_SCADA_*.csv / .xlsx) could not be downloaded from any reachable host. Only the generator, the network models and the leak ground truth are recoverable.

L-TOWN_v2_Real.inp contains 104 demand patterns of length 105120 at a 300 s pattern timestep, i.e. exactly 365.0 days. dataset_configuration.yalm requests 2018-01-01 -> 2019-12-31 (210240 steps). EPANET/WNTR pattern indexing wraps modulo pattern length, so a two-year run reproduces the 2018 demand series verbatim in 2019. Verified empirically: pattern.at(t) == pattern.at(t + 105120*300) for all sampled patterns and offsets. Consequence: any dataset regenerated from this published artefact has identical demands in both years, which is very likely NOT true of the official published SCADA and which removes demand uncertainty from the 2019 test set.
critical_findings.verification: src/audit_data.py records pattern_length_histogram and max_pattern_span_days per .inp file.

critical_findings.finding: The published dataset_generator.py applies NO measurement noise. It defines self.unc_range = np.arange(0, 0.25, 0.05) but never uses it, indicating the released generator is not the exact version that produced the published SCADA. The official noise specification lives in the rules PDF, which is on a blocked host.

The 2019 leak ground truth (link IDs, start/end/peak times, diameters) is stored in the SAME files as the 2018 configuration (dataset_configuration.yalm) and in leakages_info.yalm. It was therefore visible during the mandatory data-inventory step, before FROZEN_PROTOCOL.json existed. Mitigation is procedural and code-level, not informational: no threshold, hyperparameter, sensor subset or FO criterion is derived from any 2019 quantity, and the freezing code reads only 2018-derived artefacts. This exposure is recorded rather than concealed.
